question: On a video, what should Shift Z do?
context: Two things you asked for want the same key. The punch-in mock prints Shift Z beside Punch in; your timeline zoom request on 2026-09-28 named Shift Z for Zoom to Fit. One key can only do one thing, so today Shift Z is Punch In and the timeline fits on backslash.

options.label: Punch In, as the mock
options.summary: Shift Z punches in on the box you drew on the picture, as the punch-in mock prints it. The timeline fits itself to the whole video on backslash, which is Premiere's key for it. This is how it works today, so nothing more is built.
pros: Backslash is what a Premiere editor already presses
cons: Final Cut editors reach for Shift Z to fit the timeline and get a punch-in instead
options.mitigation: Zoom Timeline to Fit sits in the View menu and the timeline right-click with backslash printed beside it.

options.label: Fit the timeline, as you asked
options.summary: Shift Z fits the timeline to the whole video, Final Cut's key and the one you named on 2026-09-28. Punch In keeps its menu row and right-click row with no key, like Freeze Frame.
pros: What you asked for by name
A Final Cut editor's hand already knows it
Fitting is pressed far more often than punching in
cons: Departs from the key the punch-in mock prints
Punch In has no key at all
options.mitigation: Punch In stays one click away in the Clip menu and on the picture's right-click.
